source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Hardware Status" -> "Sensors"
Compare each sensor's reading and setting with BMC sensor spec.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES assumes that a literal `TEMP_DCSCM` lookup uniquely identifies the target, but does not define which DCSCM component/instance or sensing point owns it, validate units/scaling/threshold capabilities, correlate the WebUI or compare to Project SPEC. Its fallback is truncated despite the `FULL` claim and its authentication parameters are unsafe assumptions.

V3.1 adds module FRU/topology binding, distinguishes board-local temperature from ambient reference, requires threshold-capability evidence rather than forcing all limits to exist and gates the shared Script on an immutable reviewed revision.

original_test_intent: Verify that the temperature sensor for the intended DCSCM component and instance is human-readable in Hardware Status > Sensors and that its identity, board-local reading, units, health state and implemented thresholds match the DCSCM/platform sensor specification.
original_method: Bind `TEMP_DCSCM` to an exact DCSCM FRU/board instance and sensing location, collect its complete supported SDR/API record and matching WebUI row, then compare each applicable field with the versioned component specification under the recorded operating condition. No log deletion, threshold write or forced temperature is needed.
manual_activity: The hardware/FAE owner identifies the exact DCSCM FRU or board instance, sensor placement and expected thermal limits for the current chassis/load. Automation can perform read-only SDR/API/WebUI capture and comparison; a human resolves topology or labeling ambiguity and determines whether an independent physical reference is meaningful for this board-local sensor.
required_inputs: Exact DCSCM product/FRU/serial or instance, physical location/topology and relevant component/BMC firmware revisions
Stable sensor number/name/type/entity/instance and mapping to DCSCM inventory plus Hardware Status > Sensors row
Expected component-local range, Celsius scaling/rounding, sensor accuracy/tolerance, operating-load/airflow condition and update period
Implemented threshold capability mask, lower/upper limits, hysteresis, alarm/health state and unavailable/not-readable semantics
Authoritative DCSCM sensor specification and optional approved on-board/physical reference method if the spec requires independent accuracy validation
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned readable `sensor.git` revision/checksum or approved manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL or system logs; diagnostic history can explain a DCSCM thermal state and is unrelated to read-only field validation.
Do not infer DCSCM meaning, instance or physical sensor location from the label. Require FRU/topology mapping and stop on multiple DCSCM modules, aliases or mismatched entity metadata.

Do not compare the board-local DCSCM temperature directly to room ambient unless the specification defines that equivalence; record chassis load/airflow and use the specified expected range/reference.
Do not require or invent unsupported thresholds. Validate the SDR capability mask and treat specified not-applicable fields distinctly from missing required data.
Do not heat/cool the module, obstruct airflow, change thresholds or acknowledge alarms. Active thermal behavior requires a separately approved test and recovery envelope.

Do not truncate fallback output, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or run the inaccessible Script before immutable review. Stop without automatic retry on identity, threshold, freshness or UI/OOB ambiguity.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the BMC/DCSCM FRU/topology and exact sensor mapping, client and Script before collection; record component firmware, chassis load/airflow and BMC time.
Capture the complete raw SDR/API object with identity, current reading, units, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, status and timestamp, then capture the matching unchanged WebUI row.
Compare applicable fields with the versioned DCSCM specification and approved tolerance/operating condition, reporting unsupported, unavailable, stale or mismatched data separately.
Preserve raw and redacted evidence, verify no mutation occurred and never clear logs, force temperature, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact DCSCM component/instance, sensor placement and authoritative specification for the platform topology.
Define expected operating-condition range, accuracy/tolerance, threshold capabilities, status/freshness rules and any independent reference requirement; approve the Script/tool.
Review component/UI/OOB/spec discrepancies and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only a possible read after exact component and sensor identity are proven. It cannot establish DCSCM topology, specification or WebUI equality, truncates fallback data and exposes unsupported credential/cipher assumptions, so the `FULL`/readability claim is not substantiated.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Resolve the exact DCSCM FRU/instance and stable sensor identity, capture the complete supported SDR/API object through protected access and the matching WebUI row, then compare capability-aware reading/threshold/status fields with the component specification and recorded operating condition.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_DCSCM, Hardware Status > Sensors, reading/setting comparison, readability/spec Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; no active thermal stimulus is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Join DCSCM FRU/topology, canonical sensor identity and WebUI row, then perform a capability-aware field comparison against the component-local thermal specification at a documented load/airflow state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact DCSCM instance, chassis topology, BMC/SDR build and component firmware named by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record DCSCM FRU/firmware, BMC firmware, SDR package, WebUI, client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: DCSCM/platform sensor map and thermal limits, SDR definition, WebUI field schema and Project topology/specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact component ownership, board-local sensing context, capability-aware thresholds, full evidence and protected access while avoiding destructive setup.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A current readable value does not prove response under heat/load, alarm transitions, threshold persistence or protective action; those remain separate unverified functional tests.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: DCSCM/topology map, sensor/spec/condition matrix, threshold capabilities/freshness, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence rules.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Aliases or multiple modules can misbind evidence; component-local temperatures depend on airflow/load; UI caching and OEM scaling can produce legitimate presentation differences.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported Redfish/OEM telemetry interface instead of ipmitool when it records the preserved command, actual interface/version, reason, engineer approval, stable field equivalence and any UI/ipmitool coverage gap. A reference on another component cannot replace the exact DCSCM sensor unless the thermal specification explicitly maps them.
expected_evidence: Target BMC/chassis and exact DCSCM FRU/serial/instance/topology/component-firmware identity
Stable sensor-to-DCSCM/UI mapping plus complete raw SDR/API identity, capability, reading, units, thresholds/hysteresis, status and timestamp
Redacted Hardware Status > Sensors evidence tied to the same component and refresh time
Versioned DCSCM/platform expected range/threshold/status matrix, documented load/airflow condition and approved tolerance calculation
Pinned Script commit/checksum/content review or approved alternate method and credential-safe command audit
No-clear/no-write/no-stimulus/no-retry proof, BMC/component health, discrepancies/limitations and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Sensor Page procedure and Criteria consistently define read-only DCSCM temperature/spec validation. Exact component ownership, expected limits and threshold capabilities are Project/vendor readiness inputs rather than contradictory operations.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target class and read-only comparison are clear. DCSCM instance, sensor mapping, specification and Script/tool can be supplied, so this is PACKAGE rather than permanent BLOCKED; collection is gated until they are resolved.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE and rejects literal-name/truncated output absent component identity, UI correlation, spec and protected access.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification while adding FRU/topology binding, board-local thermal context, threshold capability masks and immutable Script governance.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists reasoning with exact component ownership and capability-aware field-level evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents data from the wrong DCSCM instance or an ambient sensor from satisfying the case and prevents unsupported thresholds or stale UI values from being treated as correct component health.
independent_technical_reasoning: DCSCM is a component-scoped target, so a temperature value is meaningful only after the sensor is bound to the correct FRU/instance and its physical sensing point. Board-local temperature follows component load and airflow, not necessarily room ambient. The SDR capability mask determines which limits are valid; therefore completeness means all applicable fields are verified, not that every nominal threshold slot contains a number.
